title: India chairs BRICS in 2026: the trade union track
author: Editorial Desk
summary: Where the BRICS Trade Union Forum fits.
body:
BRICS, originally Brazil, Russia, India and China, with South Africa joining in 2010, has since expanded. India holds the **chair of BRICS in 2026**.

## The labour track

Within BRICS there is a **Labour and Employment Working Group** and a **Labour and Employment Ministers' meeting**. Alongside, the **BRICS Trade Union Forum (TUF)** brings together national trade union centres of member countries. It meets before or around the summits and adopts a declaration for the leaders.

## Who takes part from India

BMS takes part among India's trade union centres in the BRICS Trade Union Forum and in the ILO. In 2026, as the Indian chair, BMS was to host the **15th BRICS Trade Union Forum Summit**, which this blog reports in a later post.

## Why it matters

- Member countries are major labour markets, and rules that they agree on on **social protection, migration, technology** and **just transition** influence the wider world.
- Trade unions can bring workers' priorities to ministers and leaders.

## The BMS note

BMS has said at such forums that a global economic order must be **worker-centric**, in line with its slogan, *Workers unite the world.*
